title: KV-quant scratchbook — small runs and prompt stress-tests
content:
Quick context:
- Goal: micro-validate how low-bit quantization (Q8, Q4) interacts with KV cache behavior and prompt-prefix stability for multi-turn chat loads. Want to catch failure modes early (stale KV pointers, token hallucinations, throughput regressions).
- This is a scratchbook: short runs, noisy notes, TODOs. Not a polished runbook.

Runs executed (local node, A100s emulated with quant profiles):
1) exp-kv-q8-2026-03-26-a
   - model: llama-2-13B-like (open-checkpoint, int8 profile built on top of baseline kernels)
   - config: qtype=Q8-columnwise, kv-cache=true, batch=1, max_new_tokens=256
   - prompt set: short chat (3-turn), medium context (1k prefix), prompt variations A,B (see prompt block)
   - observations: throughput ~ 210 tok/s, p50 latency generation step ~ 27ms; occasional "kv-miss" logging at step ~98 for long prefix (investigate alignment w/ batching). Output quality close to baseline on top-3 tokens but more repetition on long-turns.

2) exp-kv-q4-2026-03-27-b
   - model: same checkpoint w/ Q4f16 fallback kernels
   - config: qtype=Q4f16, kv-cache=true, batch=1, max_new_tokens=256
   - observations: throughput ~ 340 tok/s (big win), p50 step ~ 18ms; but two failure cases: (a) prompt continuation drift at turn 4 (coherent but adds unrelated facts), (b) rare segmentation warning from fused-kernel on step ~47. Affected only when using prompt set C (long instructions + embedded code).

3) exp-kv-q4-nocache-2026-03-28-c
   - same as (2) but kv-cache=false to isolate quality effect
   - observations: quality drift still present (so not purely KV corruption), but latency worse (obvious). Hypothesis: quantized matrix ops change conditioning for longer prefixes -> affects attention scaling.

Prompt sets (kept small to iterate):
- Prompt A (short chat): user: "Plan a 3-step onboarding for a new engineer joining infra team."
- Prompt B (multi-step instruction): long bullet list + a follow-up question asking to add edge-case tests.
- Prompt C (code-mixing): instruction with a 200-token code block in the middle (likely triggers longer attention windows + KV reuse).

Quick notes / oddities:
- Seen: "kv-miss" counter spikes correlated with small bursts in request rate (0.5s inter-arrival). Might be a race between cache insert and read path. Add instrumentation to log insertion timestamp + read timestamp for offending keys.
- Q4 drift persists when setting seed=42 (so not a sampling fluke).
- Re-running the same seed on full-float baseline shows no drift -> likely quantization numerical conditioning.
- Segfault-like fused-kernel warning only reproducible when using mixed-batched clients (batch sizes 1 and 4 concurrently) -> suspicious scheduling/kernel selection bug.

Commands used (local harness):
- python microbench/run_eval.py --model=... --quant=q4f16 --kv-cache --prompt-set=prompts/C --seed=42 --log-level=debug
- ./scripts/collect_kv_trace.sh exp-kv-q4-2026-03-27-b >> traces/exp-kv-q4-27b.trace

Preliminary hypotheses to test:
- H1: Q4f16 reduces numeric headroom on attention logits -> underflows or increased softmax saturation for long context leading to repetition. Test by increasing attention temperature and comparing saliency maps.
- H2: KV cache insertion race condition under mixed client bursts. Add per-key locking or timestamp checks and re-run inter-arrival stress test.
- H3: fused-kernel seg fault due to kernel selection mismatch for q4 vs fused int path; try forcing slower kernel family as a control to confirm.

Immediate next experiments (prioritized):
- Run exp-kv-q4-ctrl: same as exp 2 but force kernel_family=slow_scalar to confirm kernel-related artifact (low overhead but diagnostic).
- Add micro-eval measuring attention distribution shift: capture logits for first 8 heads at steps {1,32,128,200} and compare L2 distance between baseline and quant runs.
- Reproduce kv-miss by running bursty client harness (0.1s/0.7s jitter) and capturing timestamps.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Add KV insertion timestamp/log id in runtime (patch small, target minimal perf hit). Link PR to this doc.
- [ ] Spin up deterministic replay harness reusing recorded inputs (so we can replay identical inter-arrival pattern).
- [ ] Sync with Maya on microbench metric dashboard: add per-step latency and kv-miss counter graph.
- [ ] Ask Noah to eyeball fused-kernel warning logs (PR #1423 reference) and see if scheduling changes correlate.

Questions for the team / Slack message draft:
"Quick heads-up: hitting a repeaty-drift in Q4 runs (exp-kv-q4-2026-03-27-b). Not sure if numerical conditioning or kernel scheduling — Maya, can you add kv-miss counters to the micro dashboard? Noah, can you glance at PR 1423 kernel selection traces? Putting together small repro harness now. Will post traces in #aml-ops."

Longer-term notes:
- If Q4 gives consistent perf wins but marginal quality regressions on long-turns, consider hybrid: use Q4 for short-turn / low-temp traffic and fall back to Q8/FP for chat sessions where context > N tokens. Need gating logic in smart-routing to pick quant profile by route.
- Consider adding a "quantization validation" job in Optimize that runs a small suite of prompts (A,B,C) with traffic-shaped replay and flags regressions automatically.

References and links to half-formed ideas:
- idea: per-request "quantization safety" flag: run a 2-token lookahead using lighter precision to check for catastrophic logits before full generation (expensive, but could be sampled).
- draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1423 (kernel-selection logs)
- jira: JIRA-AML-487 (kv-cache instrumentation)

End-of-day brain dump. Next touch: run exp-kv-q4-ctrl and attach traces to JIRA-AML-487.

-- S.R.
